newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to deport thousands of Bulgarians.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to deport thousands of Bulgarians.

text.p: Turkey is planning to deport tens of thousands of Bulgarians whose visas have expired, an interior ministry official told Reuters on Friday.

"A directive has been sent from the prime minister's office to local governors. It foresees the deportation of those who came in from Bulgaria after January 1, 1993, and who have not yet left despite their visas running out," the official said.
The official said the directive concerned around 70,000 Bulgarians, but a security official directly involved in the directive refused to give any figure.

The ministry official said Turkey had agreed to give citizenship to ethnic Turks from Bulgaria in 1989. This lasted until 1993. The large number of arrivals after that date made it impossible to ignore the breaching of that rule, he said.

Many fled Bulgaria following Sofia's forced assimilation of ethnic Turks -- the interior ministry said in a statement that about 250,000 had been granted Turkish citizenship. But Turco-Bulgarian relations have improved since then and allegations of ill-treatment by Sofia subsided.
